newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds firm as Greenspan shadow passes.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds firm as Greenspan shadow passes.

text.p: Irish bonds firmed in late trade on Thursday as Ireland recouped some of Wednesday's losses, incurred in the wake of Fed Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony to Congress, dealers said.
But dealers said a lack of bid interest had prevented Irish bonds from rebounding from Greenspan's comments as convincingly as German bunds and UK gilts had done.

International bond markets dipped on Wednesday after U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan gave an upbeat assessment of the U.S. economy but said he was concerned about inflation risks and the buoyant equity market.
He said the Fed may raise interest rates before inflation picks up to ensure that the economy stayed on an even keel and that the nearly six-year-old expansion continues.

"The shadow of Greenspan has passed to a large extent. But Germany is up half-a-percent on the day and we should be up more than we are. There just has not been much interest in the Irish market," one dealer said.

By 1620 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was up 15 pence from Wednesday's close at 103.15 to yield 5.70 percent while the key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 was also up 15 pence from the close at 111.15 to yield 6.38 percent.
